# `Q-15-1` — Duplicate Crossref Identifier

> A crossref identifier (such as a `fig-`/`tbl-` label or an
> explicit `#id`) is defined more than once in the same document.

## What this means

Cross-references resolve by identifier: when you write `@fig-plot`,
Quarto looks up the one element whose id is `fig-plot` and links to
it with the right number ("Figure 3"). For that to be unambiguous,
each crossref id must be **unique within a document**.

This error fires when the same id is assigned to two (or more)
elements — two figures both labeled `#| label: fig-plot`, two divs
both carrying `{#fig-plot}`, and so on. The diagnostic underlines
**both** occurrences: the first definition and the duplicate.

Quarto keeps the **first** occurrence in the crossref index and
skips numbering the duplicate, so the render still completes — but
any `@fig-plot` reference would be ambiguous, and the duplicated
`id` produces invalid HTML (two elements sharing one `id`).

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **Copy-paste** — a figure or table block was duplicated and its
  `label:` / `#id` was not changed.
- **The same example shown twice** — e.g. the same figure presented
  in two tabs of a `panel-tabset` (one per engine), both keeping the
  original label.
- **A generated label collides** — an auto-derived id happens to
  match one you wrote by hand.

## How to fix

Give one of the targets a different identifier so each is unique:

- For computational figures/tables, change the `#| label:` option
  (e.g. `fig-plot-jupyter` and `fig-plot-knitr`).
- For explicit ids, change the `{#fig-plot}` attribute.

Then update any `@`-references to point at the id you intend. If the
two elements really are the same figure shown two ways and you do
not need to cross-reference one of them, you can remove the label
from that one instead.
